title: Variables & Naming Rules
subtitle: Variables are the absolute foundation of Python. This week covers what a variable is, how Python stores data in memory, and the five strict rules for naming them — rules that examiners love to test directly.
learningOutcome: Variables are the absolute foundation of Python. This week covers what a variable is, how Python stores data in memory, and the five strict rules for naming them — rules that examiners love to test directly.

content.text: A variable is a named location used to store data in memory. It acts as a container for holding values that can be referenced and manipulated. You create one by giving it a name and assigning a value with the = sign.
# Creating a variable ECE = 258 print(ECE) # Output: 258
Think of a variable like a labelled jar — the jar has a name ("Sugar") and holds something inside. The name is the label; the value is what's inside.

topics.title: The Five Rules for Naming Variables

subtopics.title: The Five Rules for Naming Variables

content.text: Rule 1 — Valid Characters Only: Variable names can only contain letters (a–z, A–Z), digits (0–9), and underscores (_). Nothing else.
Rule 2 — Cannot Start with a Digit: The name cannot start with a number.
Rule 3 — Python is Case Sensitive: ECE, ece, Ece are three different variables.
Students_ECE = 258 half_ECE = Students_ECE / 2 print(half_ECE) # Output: 129.0 print(half_ece) # NameError: name 'half_ece' is not defined
Rule 4 — No Reserved Keywords: Words like if, else, elif, for, while, def, return cannot be variable names. But you can modify them: else_1 is fine.
Rule 5 — No Special Characters: Characters like #, !, @, % are not allowed.
Bonus Rule — Be Descriptive: Use student_count instead of x. Use total_area instead of ta.

Common mistake — Only listing 3 or 4 rules — the question asks for five. Also: mixing cases accidentally (defining half_ECE then typing half_ece ). And using else or if as variable names — fix by appending a number: else_1 .

Exam answer — write this if asked:
Enumerate five conditions for naming a perfect variable: (1) valid characters only, (2) cannot start with a digit, (3) case sensitive, (4) no reserved keywords, (5) no special characters.
